voci.titolo: Fed’s Waller Says September Rate Decision Hinges on August CPI
voci.riassunto: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said his next decision on interest rates will be “heavily influenced” by August inflation data due next week, adding it may not take much to nudge him toward supporting a rate hike at the Fed’s upcoming policy meeting.

voci.titolo: 'Danger zone of extreme weather': UN warns of supersized El Niño set to hit global economy and markets
voci.riassunto: Latest modeling shows high risks of floods, drought and extreme heat persisting until February 2027.

voci.titolo: Rising Yields Seen Pushing Companies to Sell Bonds Sooner
voci.riassunto: Wall Street dealers were already bracing for a potential record in September for high-grade US corporate bond sales, and recent surging yields may give the blue-chip companies even more reason to borrow now before funding costs rise further.

voci.titolo: Retail Gilt Buying Jumps After Yields Touch Highest in Decades
voci.riassunto: British savers have sharply upped their purchases of UK government bonds this week as a selloff lifted yields to multi-decade highs.

voci.titolo: Equities Show No Real Signs of Discomfort on Yields, Says Principal’s Shah
voci.riassunto: Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management, says the factors behind higher bond yields are “not something that would really stop markets in their track.” (Source: Bloomberg)

voci.titolo: Global Bond Retreat Slows as High Yields Tempt Investors
voci.riassunto: Global bonds traded mixed as yields near multi-decade highs proved hard for some investors to resist, even as climbing energy prices kept markets on edge.

voci.titolo: Hungary Central Bank Turns to Police on Overpriced Property
voci.riassunto: The National Bank of Hungary pressed charges over fresh instances of suspected embezzlement under its previous governor, related to a series of allegedly overpriced property acquisitions.

voci.titolo: Yen Rallies as Intervention, BOJ Rate Risk Weigh on Wary Traders
voci.riassunto: The yen jumped sharply for a second day, reversing a month of gradual decline, as traders lifted bets on Japanese interest-rate hikes and were on high alert to the risk of authorities wading back into the market to boost the currency.

voci.titolo: South Korea's semiconductor exports just tripled year-over-year. Is it too much of a good thing?
voci.riassunto: If growth were to slow in the semiconductor sector, would the slowdown take the Korean economy with it?

voci.titolo: World’s Unusually High Dollar Exposure Risks Fueling Selloff
voci.riassunto: Sift through the filings of pension funds and insurers around the world and one thing stands out: some of the biggest holders of US assets have little protection against a weaker dollar, leaving the currency at risk of steeper declines if sentiment suddenly turns.

voci.titolo: Stocks Steady as Bond Yields Stabilize; Yen Gains: Markets Wrap
voci.riassunto: Stocks fluctuated as bond yields retreated from multi-year highs. The yen surged 1.8% against the dollar as traders lifted bets on Japanese interest-rate hikes, while remaining wary of intervention risk.

voci.titolo: Private payrolls rose by 38,000 in August, less than expected, ADP reports
voci.riassunto: Though job creation held positive, August was the smallest gain since January and reflective of a broader slowdown in the labor market.

voci.titolo: Euro zone inflation is back above 3%. Higher interest rates are likely to follow
voci.riassunto: The European Central Bank is seen hiking rates in September as the Iran war raises energy costs in the region.

voci.titolo: Bank of England chief warns new AI models threaten global financial stability
voci.riassunto: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey has warned that frontier AI could materially increase cyber risks to the global financial system.

voci.titolo: India’s economy expands 7.8% in fiscal first quarter, beating estimates
voci.riassunto: The economy was driven by a strong performance in the financial, real estate, information technology and professional services sectors.

voci.titolo: China's factory activity shrinks for second straight month, contracting less than expected
voci.riassunto: China's manufacturing activity shrank for a second straight month, keeping pressure on Beijing to support the economy as growth loses momentum.

voci.titolo: Singapore tackles finances and culture to avert a demographic crisis
voci.riassunto: One challenge for policy makers is that success on many measures won't show up immediately.

voci.titolo: K, C or E? Why economists can’t agree on the shape of today’s economy
voci.riassunto: Economists have long viewed the post-pandemic economy as "K"-shaped. That consensus has now evaporated.
